title: Drive organic user acquisition and viral cohort referral loops for Zedu
description: Transform active students, mentors, and bootcamp directors into an unpaid growth engine. This goal creates in-product study invite loops, instructor referral incentives, and shareable cohort showcase mechanics to drive sign-ups through organic word-of-mouth and network effects.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: In-product peer study invite mechanics and shareable project showcase links
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
Build the foundational viral loop to turn active cohort participants into new Zedu users. Today, learners and instructors collaborate inside Zedu, but when they want to share their work with peers, prospective students, or hiring managers, they have no public-facing shareable view, forcing them to screenshot or export.

Evidence (checked on https://zedu.chat/products/channels and /products/buzz): channel links and Buzz sessions require prior authentication and enrollment, creating a closed wall that stops organic word-of-mouth discovery.

Deliver:
1. Product specification and wireframes for 'Public Showcase & Study Links' allowing students to generate view-only, branded cohort project links with a prominent 'Start your cohort on Zedu' banner.
2. In-app viral trigger flows for instructors: after concluding a course module or capstone, prompt a 1-click 'Invite Guest Reviewers/Mentors' flow that seamlessly provisions guest accounts.
3. K-factor measurement rubric and virality tracking instrumentation specifying events (share_link_created, guest_invite_sent, referral_signup_completed) to measure viral loop coefficient.

Why it helps: transforms daily cohort usage into natural outward exposure, driving organic signups without ad spend.

Boundaries: proposed product specifications, micro-copy, and wireframe documentation only; no direct codebase changes, no external prospect outreach.

The accepted showcase approach already defines future share/invite instrumentation and a K-factor rubric; this proposal adds an actual pre-change aggregate baseline and locates the current loss between invitation and active use. Those are different evidence from assuming proposed public showcases will work. Its explicit check of which events are already logged is important: no baseline should be invented when events are absent. Product-team aggregate access is a real dependency, not something public page browsing can prove.

pendingIdeas.title: Set consent, privacy and removal rules before public cohort showcases
pendingIdeas.description: Before any public project or study link is designed, define what is private by default and what a learner may choose to share. Specify who can create a link, whether it reveals names or cohort details, how mixed-consent group work is handled, how long a link remains available, how it can be revoked, and who handles a removal request. Test five synthetic cases: a learner under 18, a group project with one person opting out, a forwarded link, a learner leaving the cohort, and a request to remove work. Deliver a decision table, consent and share-confirmation copy, a removal procedure, and a list of product questions the team must answer. Treat public sharing as a proposed feature, not something Zedu already supports; no real learner content or public link is created without team and learner approval. This adds a privacy and trust layer to the accepted invite-loop measurement and showcase mechanics without repeating their referral events or wireframes.

The channels page (zedu.chat/products/channels) and Buzz page (zedu.chat/products/buzz) confirm the product capabilities referenced. This idea is concrete and verifiable.

The accepted showcase workstream creates shareable public links, but nothing defines consent, defaults, revocation or removal. Testing synthetic cases (an under-18 learner, a group member opting out, a forwarded link) is exactly the safeguard public learner work needs.
Establishing clear consent, privacy, and takedown mechanisms protects student safety while enabling viral cohort showcase loops.
